narrative.overview:
The interface is painted the way a parking deck is painted. An asphalt-charcoal shell carries a line of yellow road paint. Floors are identified by a level colour, like painted pillars, and shown as a squared, stencilled floor code. The floor map is drawn as white bay lines on asphalt, and the only solid yellow on it is the driver's own slot. Content sits on a pale concrete ground in flat white panels with 1px hairlines. There are no gradients, no glass and no soft drop shadows.

Driver pages are loose and large: the floor code, the free count and the amount owed are set at stencil size inside a dark deck band. Admin pages use the same objects (floor badge, plate, painted map, hairline-split readout) in a denser grid. The exit kiosk turns the whole screen into asphalt-deep, under a yellow exit sign.

The system rejects the white-card SaaS look, with its blue buttons and green/amber/red progress bars. It replaces the earlier navy and pastel-green look completely; none of those values remain.
keyCharacteristics: An asphalt shell with a 4px yellow paint rule along the edge that meets the content.
Flat colour throughout. Depth comes from asphalt against concrete against white, never from shadow.
Floors are carried by level colour and the square floor badge, repeated at every size.
Yellow is scarce and always means "your action, your place, your slot".
Status is always a word with a fill or line treatment, never colour alone.
Thai first: comfortable 1.65 body leading, no tracking on Thai text, and tabular figures for money, counts and times.

rules.name: The Reserved Paint Rule
rules.body: Yellow as a fill means one of three things: the primary action, the active item, or the driver's own slot. Apart from those, it appears only as structural paint (the shell rule, the wordmark tile, focus, selection, the kiosk exit sign) or as a mark on asphalt (an arrow, an icon in an asphalt tile, the kiosk's read-out plate). Never use it to decorate a light panel.

rules.name: The Pillar Rule
rules.body: Level colours belong to floors. A level colour on anything that is not a floor (a chart series, a category, a button) breaks the wayfinding.

rules.name: The Word-Plus-Fill Rule
rules.body: Every status is spoken. Map bays have a fill or line state (open lines = ว่าง, grey block = มีรถ, dashed lines = ถูกจอง, yellow = ช่องของคุณ) plus a word in the title and the legend. Floor fullness is always a word (ว่างมาก / ใกล้เต็ม / เต็ม) next to its colour.

rules.name: The Dark-Ground Variant Rule
rules.body: On asphalt, use `ok-lt` and `bad-lt`, never `ok` and `bad`.

rules.name: The Stencil-for-Numbers Rule
rules.body: A floor code, a plate, an amount or a count is always set in Chakra Petch with tabular figures. Body text never is.

rules.name: The Untracked Thai Rule
rules.body: Don't add letter-spacing to Thai text. The only tracking in the system is `tracking-wide` on plate characters and `tracking-tight` on the wordmark.

rules.name: The Painted-Not-Lifted Rule
rules.body: If something needs to stand out, change its paint (asphalt against white, or yellow against asphalt). Don't lift it with a shadow or blur it with glass.

dos: Do take every colour from the `@theme` tokens in `app/globals.css`.
Do put the 4px Line Yellow rule on the edge of the asphalt shell that meets the content.
Do show every floor with a FloorBadge in its level colour, at whichever size fits.
Do pair every status colour with a word: ว่าง / มีรถ / ถูกจอง, ว่างมาก / ใกล้เต็ม / เต็ม.
Do set plates, amounts, counts and times in Chakra Petch with tabular figures.
Do keep 6px corners on controls, 8px on panels and 3px on bay furniture.
Do draw every floor map at the same bay scale.
Do use a diagonal hazard stripe (Asphalt Deep and Line Yellow, 8px bands) where a real car park would paint one, as on the kiosk exit sign.
donts: Don't use yellow on anything except the primary action, the active item, the driver's own slot and the structural paint.
Don't use a level colour for anything that is not a floor.
Don't show status with colour alone.
Don't add drop shadows, smooth gradients or glass. Depth is tonal.
Don't return to white SaaS cards with blue buttons and green/amber/red progress bars, or to the old navy and pastel-green palette.
Don't add a second entrance animation; deck-in is the only one.
